name: Magnetohydrodynamic Shear Pistol MHSP-2 'Riptide'
description: The MHSP-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic field that interacts violently with the conductive saline content of biological tissue. When the field engages a target, it induces opposing directional currents through fluid-dense regions — primarily muscle bellies, joint capsules, and organ tissue — creating a shearing force that tears tissue longitudinally without penetrating the skin. The effect is functionally similar to a severe internal strain injury distributed across a limb or torso segment in under a tenth of a second.
specifications:
length: 29 cm
weight: 1.6 kg
power source: Zheng-Dao ZD-Flux cell (compact MHD)
effective range: 4–35 m
field aperture: Variable, 15–40 cm diameter at target
discharge rate: Semi-automatic, 0.8 second recycle
shots per cell: 34
housing: Polymer-ceramic composite, field-isolated grip
tactical_use: The MHSP-2 is a compliance and incapacitation weapon when operated at standard settings, capable of dropping a target by destroying muscular cohesion in a limb without lethal injury. At maximum aperture compression, operators can concentrate the shear field to rupture deep connective tissue and cause joint dislocation. Security teams use it for non-lethal extraction of high-value targets where physical integrity matters. Closed-field operators — bodyguards, detention specialists — carry it as a primary sidearm in environments where projectile weapons are scannable but energy sidearms require higher licensing.
cultural_context: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets the MHSP-2 openly to licensed security contractors as a 'humane restraint solution,' and its presence on a guard's hip is a status signal — it says the carrier works for someone who wants live captives, not corpses. In GLMZ's debt-collection economy, MHSP-2 operators are called 'pullers' — a term that has drifted from the weapon's physics to a professional designation. The weapon is also common in underground fighting arenas where promoters want dramatic incapacitations rather than deaths.
story_hooks: A series of kidnappings in the financial district share a signature — victims are found with characteristic internal shear injuries but no external marks, suggesting MHSP-2 use by a highly organized extraction team.

A licensed 'puller' approaches the party for help: their MHSP-2 was remotely bricked mid-contract by Zheng-Dao, stranding them in a hostile situation — and now they want to know why the manufacturer killed their weapon.
An underground fight promoter is running MHSP-2-equipped enforcers to rig bouts, and a fighter who survived an 'accidental' incapacitation wants justice.
Zheng-Dao Bioelectric is quietly recalling a batch of MHSP-2 units with a firmware anomaly that causes the shear field to invert — instead of pulling tissue apart, it compresses it catastrophically.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, forward-swept pistol with an aggressive wedge profile. The barrel assembly features a distinctive bulbous emitter shroud that widens toward the muzzle—this is the field projection aperture. The overall silhouette suggests kinetic purpose without traditional ballistic geometry. Compact and purposeful, with an almost organic curve to the frame.
physical_description.dimensions: Length 29 cm, barrel to grip; emitter shroud approximately 8 cm in diameter at widest point; grip height 10 cm. Total profile roughly 12 cm wide at the aperture housing.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but manageable—1.6 kg settles as a balanced handful. The rear grip is weighted slightly forward, suggesting the power cell sits just ahead of the trigger guard. Feels dense without being unwieldy; designed for sustained low-light operations.
physical_description.primary_material: Polymer-ceramic composite frame with integrated field-isolation grip. The emitter shroud appears to be a hybrid ceramic matrix—lighter than steel but thermally resistant. Cooling vanes run longitudinally along the barrel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with subtle brushed-titanium accents around the emitter. Wear patterns on well-used examples show bare ceramic showing through the polymer at high-stress grip points. The shroud exhibits faint heat-stress discoloration—blues and subtle oxidation—suggesting operational temperatures spike during discharge.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with accent panels in anodized copper-bronze (field-conductive markers indicating safe touch zones). Grip is matte black with textured grip panels.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with aggressive diamond-pattern texturing, designed to maintain grip even in wet or augmented-limb scenarios. Field-isolated; non-conductive outer layer. Subtle ridging at pressure points where fingers naturally rest.
distinctive_features: Bulbous ceramic emitter shroud with visible cooling radial fins
Dual LED status indicators—one blue (charge state) and one amber (aperture width)—housed just above the trigger guard
Recessed capacitor bleed-valve port on the left side of the frame (thermal management)
Micro-scale field calibration notch on the barrel (visible targeting reference for variable aperture)
Integrated ZD-Flux cell housing with faint amber glow visible through translucent access panel on the grip
Reduced-profile safety lever integrated into the trigger guard—non-protruding design for holster carry
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo stamped in block characters on the left side of the ceramic shroud. Serial plate recessed into the grip panel (compliance marking). Small Φ currency symbol etched near the aperture—pricing or authorization mark.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained examples show minimal polymer wear; field-use units display scuffed ceramic, discolored heat vents, and faint stress fractures in the composite around the grip. Operational weapons often have custom tape wraps on the grip or modified safety levers. The emitter shroud in veteran units shows pronounced heat-staining and ceramic microcracking from sustained use.
